title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA)
what: The Pazin State Archive holds the parish registers of central Istria. Two letters to this family, of 26 April and 24 June 2021, enclosed the certified copy of Josip Defranceschi's 1863 baptism and prints from the Status Animarum of Gallignana for the households of Antonius and of Giovanni Battista.
cites: MKR župe Gračišće 1841–1899, entry 23 of 1863
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01071656
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01072071
Church books ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215, Gologorica, Gračišće and Lindar
note: They charge for research and will search, certify and post a named record. The two 2021 requests cost 117 and 124 kuna including overseas postage.

title: Arolsen Archives — International Center on Nazi Persecution
what: The former International Tracing Service. Holds the wartime and displaced-persons records of some seventeen and a half million people, and 79 records under this surname — many more than the family's own copy of file D-1.505. Mined to the bottom in September 2026: the Reutlingen town list of Yugoslav nationals, the wartime sickness-fund cards in their original colour, the IRO care-and-maintenance file, and the whole of displaced-persons folder DP0758 — nineteen French occupation cards for the two brothers' households, holding Petar's photograph, the day Zdravko's family sailed for Australia, and Luise's statelessness.
cites: DP folder DP0758, reference 03010101 05 070 — nineteen cards, IRO 148.901 and 148.902
Counselling card, category CB, 28.4.51, with the entries of 22.7.49, 28.4.51 and 25.5.51
Carte d'identité de personnes déplacées no. 30040, issued 27 November 1946 to Lujza Defranceski
Tracing and documentation case no. 349.822, reference 06030302.0.349.822, 8 documents, 1954–1984 — withheld online
Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR, CM/1 files from Germany (3.2.1.1), 6 documents
note: Access requires accepting a declaration about sensitive personal data; the account holder must do that himself. Person rows in the search results are click handlers, not links, and the page images sit on a separate server that requires a referer header. The T/D tracing case is the one substantial thing still unread: eight documents spanning 1954 to 1984, withheld online for data protection and obtainable only by written request to Bad Arolsen.

title: Hrvatski državni arhiv
what: The Croatian State Archive. HDA 583 is the Pisino (Pazin) marriage register in which Carlo De Franceschi signs as a witness on 13 September 1842, giving his rank as I. R. Auscultans.
cites: HDA 583, Pisino marriages 1842–43

title: Matične knjige — Croatian parish registers
what: The baptism of Ana Kalanj at Ledenice on 3 January 1864; the baptism of Anton Rudolf at Klenovica on 20 January 1890, which gives the parents' place of origin as Gallignana in Istria; the marriage of Nodburga Defranceschi at Bakar on 27 February 1794.
note: Held as scans by the family.

title: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli and Comune di Concesio — atti di morte
what: Italian civil death registers: Pietro De Franceschi, mason, aged 44, in the civic hospital at San Daniele on 30 March 1895; Edoardo De Franceschi, former officer of Zara, aged 48, in the same hospital on 12 August 1899; Giovanni De Franceschi, aged three, at Concesio above Brescia on 15 July 1916.
cites: San Daniele del Friuli, atti di morte no. 19 (1895) and no. 28 (1899)
Concesio, atti di morte, parte II serie A (1916)

title: Antenati — Portale degli Antenati
what: The Italian state archives' genealogy portal. The Archivio di Stato di Udine has 49,184 registers on it, including 6,693 for the communes of the Tolmezzo tribunal — that is Carnia — and fifty-nine for the Comune di Mione alone. The three De Franceschi birth acts of 1809–1810 at Mione and Muina come from there.
cites: Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1809 e 1810
Nati, indice 1806–1810, sig. 12954
note: Its name search sits behind a bot check, which this archive does not bypass. Browsing the registers by place and year needs no such thing, and the images are served openly over IIIF — which is how these were read.

title: FamilySearch
what: The single largest source in this archive. Its collection «Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994» (cc 2040054) supplied the burial and baptism entries; its persona search supplied the household reconstructions, the emigrant records and the four children of Josip and Ana Kalanj; its catalogue supplied the parish-book inventory.
cites: Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994 (cc 2040054)
note:
Free with an account. Only about a quarter of that collection is name-indexed; the rest is images to be read. Nothing was bulk-downloaded. 

**On `sg30p0.familysearch.org`:** *that host is FamilySearch's own image-delivery server, not a separate body.* **An ark resolves to an apid, the apid is fetched from `sg30p0`, and what comes back is a signed S3 URL whose credential scope must be derived from `X-Amz-Date` rather than hardcoded.** *It appears in the data as a link to a film frame and is named here so that it is not mistaken for an archive of its own.*

title: Find a Grave
what: Ninety-six memorials under every spelling of the surname, from which the grave gazetteer is built. Each name on that page links to its own memorial.
note: A volunteer index, heavily weighted to the English-speaking world and Italy. Croatia is almost absent from it, and the count of one Croatian grave is a fact about the index before it is a fact about the family.

title: Wikimedia Commons
where: commons.wikimedia.org · and the credit lines it carries
what: Four public-domain works reproduced on the namesakes page: Titian's portrait of Andrea de' Franceschi (Detroit Institute of Arts); the Vasari woodcut of Piero della Francesca from the 1648 Vite; Piero's Urbino diptych; and Mariano de Franceschi's Camel Caravan at Rest.
note:
Each file is credited and linked on the namesakes page itself. 

**Three hosts in this archive's data belong to Commons rather than to this archive:** *`artgallery.yale.edu`, `www.armchairgeneral.com` and `purl.org` appear only inside the `credit` field of a Commons image record* — Yale for *Francesco de' Franceschi, Saint Mamas before Aurelian* (1450), the other two on the Dien engraving after Riesener of **général Jean-Marie-Antoine Defrance**. **They are the licence's attribution chain, not bodies this archive consulted**, and they are reproduced because a public-domain credit must travel with the image.

title: Lee Steiner, Croatia Church Books — mapped
what: A set of Google Earth overlays mapping every Croatian parish register in the FamilySearch collection to its place, with the browse link for each. Used to inventory what survives on film for Crikvenica, Ledenice, Novi Vinodolski, Grižane, Selce, Senj and Fužine.
note: Held in the family's own files as .kmz.

title: Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria: note storiche»
what: The family's own historian on his own country: 524 pages, published at Parenzo by Gaetano Coana and dedicated «alla gioventù dell'Istria». Read here end to end in September 2026 from the Internet Archive's scan. It is the source for the Seget estate's chain of owners and the Cretan origin of that branch, for the whole shape of the diocese of Pedena in which Gallignana and Gologorica sat, and for the 1764 roll of colonist families on the Seget lands. It is also, and importantly, silent about Carnia.
cites: p. 363 — the Seghetto and Giuba estate, Cuchich 1604, Valier 1623, and the de Franceschi «emigrata dall'isola di Candia»
p. 363–364, footnote 3 — Giambattista de Franceschi, deputy to the Imperial Council, and the roll of 30 April 1764
p. 484 — the parishes of the diocese of Pedena, and the chapter at Gallignana with its archpriest
p. 173 — the disputed appointment to the pieve of Gallignana, 1324–1335
p. 328–329 — the siege of Gallignana, May 1617
p. 205 — Francesco Claj, priest of Gallignana, and the Croatian translations, 1 January 1563
note: Free and complete online, which the archive had not realised. The OCR text layer is poor — accents garbled, words split at line ends, footnotes badly mangled — so page references above are approximate to the printed pagination shown in the scan, and anyone quoting should open the image.

title: «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler»
where: Atti e Memorie della Società Istriana, 1928
what: The letters in which Carlo, about 1873, sets out what his family believed about itself: that it came from Carnia and settled in Istria «intorno al 1700»; that De Franceschi still lived at Mione and Muina; that his trisavolo Giambattista built the 1711 house at Gologorica; and the blazon of the family arms.
note: The single most important narrative source in this archive.
held: texts/1978 Kobler - Memorie per la storia della citta di Fiume (Atti Rovigno 3) FULL TEXT.txt

title: Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino»
what: Carlo's son on the county the family lived in — still the standard work. With his editions of the Labin statutes, the Piran chartulary and «Gli Artizoni di Parenzo».
note: Some of the primary sources Camillo used were destroyed in the Second World War and its aftermath. For those documents his articles are now the only witness.

title: Blasonario Giuliano
what: The armorial of Venezia Giulia. Its entry «Franceschi (De) — Pisino, Moncalvo, Pola» names Carlo and Camillo and gives the family's arms; a separate entry covers the Seghetto, Capodistria and Umago branch, and others the Capodistria and Ližnjan families.
cites: Blasonario_D.pdf
Blasonario_F.pdf
note: The blazon of the Moncalvo arms is credited to «(C. de F.)» — Carlo himself — with Benedetti and de Totto supplying the tinctures. It formalises his testimony rather than confirming it independently.

title: Petar Puhmajer, «Stancija de Franceschi u Segetu kod Umaga»
what: The conservation monograph on the Seget estate: how it was bought from the Valier in 1720, how the house was built and rebuilt, and the two Istrian branches.

title: «La tenuta de Franceschi di Seghetto», la Voce del popolo
what: The Italian-language daily of Rijeka on the Seget estate: the county in Crete, the 1538 defence of Calus, Lemiores and Sabionera, the shipwreck of 1669, the hundred thousand ducats of 1716, the library of four thousand volumes and its destruction, and the arms on the tympanum. Photographs by Gianfranco Abrami.
note: Where it and the Blasonario disagree on a date, the armorial is preferred and the difference is stated.

title: Deborah Howard, «Titian's Portraits of Grand Chancellor Andrea de' Franceschi»
what: The life of Andrea de' Franceschi, born 1473, Grand Chancellor of Venice from 15 September 1529 until his death in 1552, buried at Santi Giovanni e Paolo — his embassies, his will and its five codicils, and the Titian portraits he left his nephew.

title: Josip Banić, «Venetian Istria in the Embrace of a Nascent Dominium (c. 1381 – c. 1470)»
what: A modern historian's verdict on Camillo: one of three figures who «tower» over Istrian medieval studies, and the only surviving witness to sources lost in the war. Quotes Egidio Ivetic that for medieval Istria one must rely on Benussi, Carlo De Franceschi and De Vergottini.

title: Centro di Ricerche Storiche di Rovigno — catalogue of Istrian sacred art
what: Catalogues the paintings in the chapel of Stancija Seghetto — formerly Villa De Franceschi — and records their poor condition; and a Pentecost whose patron Antonio Alisi identified as «un de Franceschi nobile di Seghetto».

title: Hrvatski plemićki zbor — the Franceschi family
what: The Croatian Noble Corps on the Zadar and Omiš descent: Niccolò received into the Hungarian-Croatian nobility by charter at Buda in 1359; the branch at Omiš from Francesca de Franceschi in the later sixteenth century; Giovanni «il Zuane» and the siege of Imotski in 1718.

title: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani
what: The biographies of Carlo De Franceschi, Camillo De Franceschi and Girolamo de' Franceschi of Koper, bishop of Corone.

title: Diocesan and press notices for Mons. Lucio Soravito de Franceschi
where: Arcidiocesi di Udine; Cathopedia; Messaggero Veneto
what: Born at Mione di Ovaro on 8 December 1939, ordained 1963, Bishop of Adria-Rovigo 2004–2015, died 6 July 2019. The evidence that the surname was still in the village of the 1679 headmen's list two hundred and sixty years later.

title: «The DeFranceschi Family Tree Album»
where: printed for the first family reunion, Crystal Springs Resort, 7–9 September 2012
what: The American branch's own history and chart, headed «started by Antonio DeFranceschi 8/6/1856 – 10/23/1924 + Maria Valhart 4/6/1867 – 1945». Eleven children, five countries. Also the description of the arms carved on the 1711 house at Moncalvo.
note: Assembled from Anton Rumac's handwritten notes and a cassette tape made by cousin Bruno. Its compiler says plainly there will be errors; where it can be checked against registers, it holds.
held: Printed album held by the family

title: The family's MacFamilyTree file
what: A database of 284 people, 114 families and 211 recorded events, with 247 photographs, catalogued and captioned by the family; last written 18 November 2021. It is the source of every portrait on this site of the Crikvenica house and of three photographs of graves. Read again in September 2026 for the parts of it that are not pictures: two ancestral lines behind Hedviga Blažević that appear in no other source here, the occupations of three generations, and one sentence of testimony about the Crikvenica house.
cites: Toma Žubrinić, born 1768 — the deepest maternal ancestor in the file
Toma Blažević, 27 January 1838 – 26 July 1907, and Tereza Pećanić
Ruža Hreljac, 13 February 1922 – 30 January 1996, of Lovre Hreljac and Dragica Vlahović
Milka Papić — «Cigar Roller / Maker»
Josip — «He built this house himself, for his family, but was lost due to family greed.»
note: Family testimony, not register evidence, and it carries the marks of it: dates that are days and months without years, a child filed under the wrong parents, a woman given her mother's death year. Where it conflicts with a register — Zdravko's death year, Josip's wife — the register is preferred and the conflict is stated on the page. Names of living people are not published.
held: An application file held by the family

title: defranceski.com
what: The roster of significant persons, the account of the four Croatian lines, the collected blazons, and the descent chart that first set out the line from Giovanni of Gologorica to Brisbane.
note: This archive absorbs its content rather than duplicating it; its hosted images are token-gated and could not be fetched, so equivalent public-domain works were sourced from Wikimedia Commons instead.

title: The Omiš and Seget photographs
what: Studio portraits of the Omiš branch — Josip and Anna with baby Ante, Zane, Frane, Anton «Toni» of 1932 — and seven photographs of the Seget villa: the 1843 façade, the tympanum with its carved arms, the crenellated tower, the rustic range and the well.

title: MyHeritage family tree export, July 2018 — SUPERSEDED
where: Held by the family — «2018-07 Defranceski.ged». Superseded by the live tree.
what: A GEDCOM of 8,286 individuals, 254 of them carrying this surname. **Retired on 7 September 2026 and not to be used again.** David: «really old and really wrong». It is the source of the Imotski mis-splice, and on 15 September it was found to be why a whole Australian branch of the family was missing from this archive — the live tree has 15,643 people in it and had held them for years. Rows in this archive still carrying a 2018 identifier are being reconciled against the live tree one by one.
cites: Anton Defranceski, b. 22 August 1944 Reutlingen, d. 28 June 1999 Ipswich
Ruža Hreljac, b. 13 February 1922 Fužine, d. 30 January 1996 Horsham
Hedviga Blažević, b. 3 August 1926 Senj, d. 30 October 2001 Johannesburg
Ivan Defranceski, b. 25 June 1925 Crikvenica, d. 30 October 1995 Senj
Josip «Pepe» Defranceski 1911–1980 and Božica Blašković 1911–1994
note: Read with care and read to the bottom. The seam where the two families are joined is set out on the Imotski page; below it the file is the best source the archive has for the twentieth-century household. Its narrative notes on the Imotski family are quoted from stariimotski.com, credited there to the archive of Captain Vjeko Franceschi.

title: Geneanet — «Urban ANTOINE's Family Tree», published by the member «carnia»
what: A Carnian researcher's tree covering the villages of the Gorto valley. It holds the only rounded De Franceschi household this archive has for Mione — five generations of the «dal Ginut» house, with trades, house-names, burial at the Pieve di Gorto, and notes written in Carnian Friulian rather than Italian. Its dates are register-precise and internally consistent, which for an online tree is unusual and suggests direct work in the Ovaro books.
cites: Francesco Arcangelo De Franceschi, «Checo dal Ginut», 5 Aug 1852 – 9 Jun 1939, tessitore contadino
Leopoldo Eugenio De Franceschi, «Poldo dal Ginut», 15 Sep 1900 – 30 Sep 1973, marangon boscador
GioBatta De Franceschi, 16 Jun 1816 – Aug 1906, and Anna Lucia Giorgis, 20 Nov 1820 – 3 Dec 1852
Maddalena Erman, daughter of Benedetto Erman, in the Giorgis ancestry
note:
Two saved pages are in the family's own files; the tree itself is behind a Geneanet login and parts need a premium account. No descent from this household to the Istrian line is claimed or shown. The member is worth writing to. 

**Blocked as of September 2026.** *HTTP 403 on every URL, including the public surname pages at `en.geneanet.org` and the tree itself at `gw.geneanet.org`, and not circumvented.* **The links are kept because they name real work; none of it has been read, and nothing here rests on it.**

title: istrianet.org — Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria», transcribed
where: Held in the family's files since November 2004 as «Defranceski History.doc»
what: A clean transcription of several chapters of Carlo's 1879 book, made from the Arnaldo Forni reprint, with maps from Egidio Ivetic's «L'Istria moderna» and biography from Benussi — both Centro di Ricerche Storiche, Rovigno. It covers the depopulation of Istria by war and plague and the repopulation by colonists, and it carries the Seget passage and the roll of 30 April 1764 in readable text.
cites: The Cuchich investiture of 1604, the Valier sale of 1623 and the de Franceschi purchase «emigrata dall'isola di Candia»
«Addì 30 Aprile 1764 Seghetto di Umago» — the roll of colonist families, corrected against this text
note: The file had been in the family's own folders for twenty-two years, unopened by this project until September 2026. It is a web capture, not a manuscript, and it is Carlo's published book rather than any family history — but it is a better text than the OCR, and the archive's transcription of the 1764 roll has been corrected from it.

title: The family's own copy of the Reutlingen displaced-persons file
what: The French-zone and IRO papers for both brothers' households, photographed by the family. It overlaps Arolsen's online folder DP0758 in part — but it also holds what Arolsen does not: the whole of Zdravko, Ruža and Anton's file, whose Arolsen index card is stamped «CM/1 destroyed». Zdravko's fiche carries his photograph; Ruža's carries a photograph of her holding the baby. It also holds two documents that change the reading of the file: the IRO director's letter of 27 May 1949 explaining the B and BJ classifications, and a health-service slip recording that Petar was screened for Brazil.
cites: A. Poignant, Director of the IRO French zone, to the Chef de Service du Wurtemberg, 27 May 1949 — «Cas de DEFRANCESKI (148.902)»
Dr S. Birietaité, Chef de Service de Santé — «passé au screening — Brésil. Rien à signaler»
Fiches individuelles 30560 (Zdravko), 30561 (Ruža), 52852 (Anton), 52850 (Ursula), 52851 (Renate), 30609 (Petar)
Identity cards of 27 November 1946, each annotated later «8/3/1949 Australie»
Stadt Reutlingen certificates of 28 February 1950 for Anton, Felix, Ivan, Zdravko and Ruža
note: Read in September 2026, after sitting unopened in the project's own folder list. Where it and the Arolsen index disagree — Ruža's birth date — three documents here agree on 13 February 1922 against Arolsen's single 2 May.

title: Anita Marin, «Oznake vlasništva i posvete na knjigama Knjižnice obitelji De Franceschi»
what: The paper that told this archive its subject's library still exists. Written by the librarian of the Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica in Zagreb who catalogued the collection. It establishes that the books and family archive of the De Franceschi of Gologorica reached the NSK after 1945, stood unprocessed for over fifty years, and now hold 2,480 catalogued items under the shelfmark PDF — Poklon De Franceschi — together with fourteen boxes and seven folders of family archive containing Carlo's and Camillo's manuscript drafts, the family correspondence, estate papers, photographs and an album.
cites: 2,480 items: 138 serials and 2,341 monographs, 1503–1945
«pronađena izbačena iz ormara i razbacana po kući» — found in 1945 thrown out of the cupboards and scattered about the house
Giulio De Franceschi, painter, Rijeka 1856 – Gologorica 1942
Seventeen stamped ex libris of Tomaso Luciani (Labin 1818 – Venice 1894)
217 of 2,341 books carry any ownership mark — the family used signatures, never a bookplate
note: Open access and free. The ResearchGate copy is behind a bot check; the journal's own PDF at morepress.unizd.hr is not. In Croatian, with an English abstract.
held: articles/2024 Marin - Oznake vlasnistva Knjiznica obitelji De Franceschi, Libellarium 15(2).pdf

title: Marin, Jurišić & Matijaca, «Arhiv obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu»
what: The published inventory of the family archive, shelfmark PDF 2.337 — fourteen boxes and nine folders, described box by box by the three librarians who arranged them. It is the document this archive was about to write to Zagreb to ask for. Among what it lists: the household accounts of Gologorica for 1925–26 and 1929–30; a lease of the second floor of the house to the parish priest in 1907; the photograph album; five boxes of correspondence including Carlo's «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler»; the personal papers of Carlo, Camillo, Gian Pietro and Giulio; and the architect's plan of the family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica.
cites: Shelfmark PDF 2.337 — 14 boxes and 9 folders, material from the 18th century to 1943
Box 6 — the photograph album, and «Maria De Franceschi, Parenzo, 187[?]»
Boxes 7–11 — «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler»; Camillo to his sister Faustina, 1886–1893
Box 12 — «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino», by the architect Giuseppe Hirsch
Folder 6 — «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897»
note: Open access at ojs.srce.hr. Croatian, with an English abstract. Found through Crossref after ResearchGate refused this session.
held: archives/2024 Marin Jurisic Matijaca - Arhiv obitelji De Franceschi NSK Zagreb, Arhivski vjesnik 67.pdf

title: Jakov Jelinčić, «Korespondencija Giovanni Kobler — Carlo De Franceschi», I–III
where: Vjesnik historijskih arhiva u Rijeci i Pazinu XXI (1977), XXII (1978), and part III
what: Kobler's side of the correspondence — the letters Carlo was answering — edited and published in three parts. Sixteen years of letters between two men who, Jelinčić notes, never managed to meet. It contains Kobler's inventory of the Defranceschi households of Fiume, his question «È forse Lei un Discendente?», and the record of Valentino Defranceschi, come from Carnia and made a citizen of Fiume in 1739.
cites: Valentino Defranceschi, «venuto dalla Carnia», citizen of Fiume 1739; the Chapel of St Helen, 1764; his tomb in the Duomo, epigraph 1785
Giovanni Antonio De Franceschi, doctor of law and municipal chancellor, d. 1727
Giovanni Battista Defranceschi, come from the County of Pisino about 1740
note: Open access on Hrčak, free. Italian letters with a Croatian editorial apparatus.
held: articles/1977, 1978 and 1981 Jelincic - Korespondencija Kobler-De Franceschi I-III, VHARP 21, 22, 24.pdf

title: Stipan Trogrlić, «Gologorica u Kronici Župe (1892.–1918.) prema zapisima župnika Ljudevita Žvačeka»
what: The parish chronicle of Gologorica for 1892–1918, as kept by the parish priest Ljudevit Žváček — on the national-political, moral-religious, economic-social and ethnographic life of the village. Žváček is the same priest to whom Giulio and Camillo de Franceschi let the second floor of their house in 1907. Croatian, with Italian and English versions of the article.
note: Open access on Hrčak. Not yet read in detail by this archive.
held: articles/Trogrlic - Gologorica u Kronici Zupe 1892-1918, VIA 32.pdf

title: Hrčak — the portal of Croatian scientific and professional journals
what: Free, open, and the place where Croatian scholarship on this family actually lives. A search for «De Franceschi» returns twenty-three items including the three NSK collection papers, the Kobler correspondence in three parts, and reviews of Camillo's history of the County of Pazin in its 2023 Croatian translation. «Gologorica» returns seven, «Gračišće» thirteen — among them the parish chronicle, the urban development of the town, the altar of the Madonna of Mercy, and the last Habsburg emperor's visit on 6 April 1918.
note: Search «De Franceschi» with the space, not «Defranceschi» — the fused spelling returns mostly Croatian rheumatology papers by an unrelated co-author. Hrčak was reachable directly where ResearchGate, Geneanet and WikiTree all served this session a bot check. Searched exhaustively for «franceschi» in September 2026: fourteen distinct articles, listed on the search register.

title: Miroslav Bertoša, «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa»
where: in «Etos i etnos zavičaja», Čakavski sabor, Pula – Rijeka 1985, pp. 177–253
what: Seventy-six pages on the De Franceschi of Gologorica by one of Croatia's leading historians of Istria — «between ethos and ethnos», on a family that was Friulian-Carnian in origin and Italian-national in politics, in a village that was Croatian in speech. It is the standing scholarly account of the household this archive's Gologorica registers reconstruct, and it is the source Trogrlić leans on for the statement that the family settled there in the seventeenth century.
cites: «furlansko-karnijske obitelji De Franceschi, koja se naselila u Gologoricu još u 17. st.» — quoted by Trogrlić
«Wallungen der Akkulturation» in the second half of the 19th century — Bertoša's conclusion, as reported by Daniela Simon (2024), who points to pp. 225 and 228
note: Still not read by this archive. It is a 1985 book chapter and not online; it would have to come from a Croatian library or by interlibrary loan. Daniela Simon's 2024 monograph cites it as «Bertoša, Miroslav: Etos i etnos zavičaja, Pula/Rijeka 1985, S. 177–253, insb. S. 225, 228», which is the sharpest pointer we have to the pages that matter. It remains the most important single thing still unread.

title: Irma Huić, «Urbanistički razvoj Gračišća u Istri»
where: Prostor 23 (2015) 2, pp. 208–221 — Faculty of Architecture, University of Zagreb
what: The first study anyone has made of how Gračišće grew — the family's own parish. It locates the bishop of Pedena's palace in the village, and the Salamon palace built facing it; and its source list points at the Franciscan cadastre of Gallignana of about 1820 at Trieste, and at the published urbaria of the County of Pazin of 1498 and the sixteenth century.
cites: «Gotovo istovremeno nasuprot biskupskoj rezidenciji gradi se palača Salamon»
ASTr, Catasto franceschino, Distretto di Pisino, Comune di Gallignana d'Istria, foglio IV sezione IV
note: Open access on Hrčak. Its Franceschi citations are all to Carlo's book of 1879 and Camillo's of 1964.

title: ANNO — Historische Zeitungen und Zeitschriften, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek
what: Full-text searchable historic Austrian newspapers, free and without registration. Istria was Austrian until 1918, so the Istrian press is in it. A search for «Defranceschi» returns 722 issues. Narrowing works: «"De Franceschi" Gallignana» returns eight, «"De Franceschi" Moncalvo» six, «"De Franceschi" Gologorica» three, and «"de Franceschi" Pisino» a hundred and thirteen. Worked through in September 2026 for the Gallignana, Moncalvo and Gologorica sets; the Pisino set is unread.

The search interface is an Angular application, but it is backed by a plain JSON endpoint, and page images come from the library's own IIIF service without a bot check — so issues can be read at full resolution. The legacy page viewer sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and was left alone. Reading is by OCR run on the page images. The engine available here has no Italian model, so it is being run in English on Italian type: it locates a passage reliably and transcribes it imperfectly. Quotations taken from ANNO on this site are marked as OCR readings, and any word the scan broke is bracketed rather than guessed. Still to do: «"de Franceschi" Pisino», 113 issues. The «Naša Sloga» issues that matter have now been read: where the presentation manifest returns 404 the IIIF image endpoint still serves the pages, which is how 25 March 1909 was recovered. 

**`data.onb.ac.at` is ANNO's permalink host, not a second body.** *An issue opens at `http://data.onb.ac.at/ANNO/<id>` — `edp18870903` is L'Eco di Pola of 3 September 1887, `igp18960111` Il giovine Pensiero of 11 January 1896.* **The Il giovine Pensiero hits cluster in January across 1893, 1894, 1895 and 1896, which looks like an annual notice rather than four stories** — the kind of pattern a hit count hides and a date list shows.

title: The State Archives of Friuli Venezia Giulia — Trieste, Udine, Gorizia, Pordenone
what: A guide to what each holds. Two things in it bear directly on this archive. The Archivio di Stato di Trieste holds the Austro-Hungarian military records — Trieste recruitment lists, navy recruitment lists and draft cards with service records — and the civil registers of the province for 1924–44 including the municipalities ceded to Yugoslavia in 1947. The Archivio di Stato di Udine holds the «Ruolo della Popolazione», the population rolls of 1836 and 1865, which give for each household the head, the parents' names, religion, date and place of birth and date of marriage — for the province that contains Mione and Ovaro.
cites: Ruolo della Popolazione, Udine province, 1836 and 1865
ASTr — Austro-Hungarian military and navy recruitment lists and draft cards
Archivio di Stato di Gorizia — Libri dei fuochi (household registers) 1830–1956, and Ventilazioni ereditarie 1755–1850
note: Data-protected records open after 75 years unless you are directly related. The state archives do not issue civil certificates. Found through a resource list the family supplied.

title: sortedbyname.com — DEFRANCESCHI
what: 127 entries drawn from the Social Security NUMIDENT and death files, state marriage and death indexes released through ReclaimTheRecords, and Ellis Island passenger manifests. Three American clusters: an Istrian one in New York, a Friulian one at Torrington and Waterbury in Connecticut, and a coal-country one in Harrison County, West Virginia. The New York group includes Basilio Defranceschi and his son Dario, born at Gallignana in 1937 — the first family this archive can trace from Gračišće to America.

Basilio Defranceschi, b. 29 September 1909, d. 15 June 1994, New York
Joseph Defranceschi, b. 12 March 1892 at Trieste, son of Anthony and Makia Valhart

title: dLib.si — the Digital Library of Slovenia
what: Free and open, and it holds runs of the Austrian Littoral periodicals — including Kandler's «L'Istria» of 1846–52, which Irma Huić cites for Gračišće. A surname search returns Slovenian notices of the family's scholarship: Camillo's «Chartularium Piranense», his «I castelli della Val d'Arsa», and a review of Carlo's history of Istria.
note: Reached without a bot check. Its value here is the periodicals rather than the notices; L'Istria has not yet been read for this family.

title: Ivan Grah, «Izvještaji pićanskih biskupa Svetoj Stolici (1589–1780)»
what: Every report the bishops of Pićan (Pedena) sent to Rome between 1589 and 1780, summarised from the Vatican archive. Pedena was the diocese of Gallignana and Gologorica, and the bishop was the temporal lord of Gologorica from about 1600. The reports give the lordship, the colonus tenants and what was done to them, the diocese's revenue, the names and ages of the clergy, and the replacement of the Glagolitic liturgy with Latin.
cites: Bishop Zara, 1606 and 1614 — lordship of Gologorica «lately» acquired
Bishop Aldrago, 1770s — «gospodar Gologorice, Škopljaka i Tupljaka»
1656 and 1661 — Juraj Kukurin, parish priest of Gologorica, aged 52
The fifteen colonus families of Tupljak, sold for sixty florins of tax
note: Free full text on the Internet Archive. The De Franceschi in its footnotes are Carlo and Camillo, cited as authorities; no member of this family appears in the text itself.

title: Internet Archive — full-text search
what: Not only the scanned books. The Archive's full-text index reaches inside them, and inside long runs of newspapers and journals that matter here: «Il Piccolo» of Trieste from 1881, «La Patria del Friuli» and the «Giornale di Udine» for Carnia, and the complete «Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno», the scholarly journal of Istrian history. Searching the surname alone returns 2,435 documents and is useless; paired with a place it becomes a finding aid.

«Defranceski» — 117 documents
note: Swept in September 2026. The search endpoint behind the site answers plain requests, so the sweep can be run by term and by place rather than page by page. Much of what the bare surname returns is a modern Italian mathematician and OCR noise; every hit used here was opened and read.

title: Giorgio Ferigo, «Le cifre, le anime. Scritti di storia della popolazione e della mobilità in Carnia»
what: The collected demographic history of Carnia by the historian who did the work on its migration. It quotes the headmen's return of 1679 in full — the document this archive's whole Carnia argument rests on — and states that the men listed in it are weavers. It also traces the «strada dei furlani» into Istria from a weaver's-shop purchase at Montona in 1511 and a Carnian's will dictated at Pedena in 1540.

«onde dire cargnel in Istria equivaleva a dire tessitore»
The 1679 return covers only the imperial county and undercounts
note: Free full text on the Internet Archive. Ferigo died in 2007; this is the posthumous collection.

title: «Ovaro: itinerari e ricerche» — with Luana Pasut, «Fonti ovaresi nell'Archivio di Stato di Udine»
where: Quaderni del Centro regionale di Catalogazione e Restauro, Villa Manin di Passariano, 1995
what: A guide to the comune of Ovaro, which contains Mione, with an inventory of what the Archivio di Stato di Udine holds for it. The inventory lists the old notarial archive by notarial seat, and under Mione stands a notary of this surname.

Napoleonic civil registers for Mione and its aggregated communes, 1806–1815

title: Mieczysław Małecki, «Przegląd słowiańskich gwar Istrji»
where: Prace Komisji Językowej nr 17, Polska Akademja Umiejętności, Kraków 1930
what: A dialect atlas of Slavic Istria with six maps, made by a Polish Slavist in the 1920s. Both of this family's parishes are survey points: Gologorica as I, 3 and Gračišće as I, 2, a — different dialect groups. It records actual words from each. It also states, against the assumption this archive had been carrying, that Moncalvo is the older name of Gologorica and the Slavic name replaced it around 1102.

The Čepić dialect wedge, cut off from its centre by the Istro-Romanian villages
note: Free on the Internet Archive, from the Toruń university library copy. Written in Polish; the dialect data are in Małecki's own phonetic transcription and are quoted here as printed.

title: «Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno»
what: The scholarly journal of Istrian history, published by the Italian research centre at Rovinj. The complete run from 1970 to 2024 is free on the Internet Archive, along with the monographs of the Collana degli Atti. It edits and prints archival material — parish registers, cadastres, town statutes — as well as articles, which is why a marriage entry from Valle in 1795 naming a De Franceschi of Gologorizza is findable in it.
cites: vol. 3 (1972) — the registers of Valle; the marriage of Piero De Franceschi of Gollogorizza and Anna Bembo, 22 January 1795
vol. 3 (1972) — Moncalvo as a nineteenth-century name for Gologorizza, and the confusion with Golaš near Valle
vol. 4 (1973) — Cervani and Ettore De Franceschi on depopulation in Venetian Istria
vol. 15 (1997) — «La popolazione dell'Istria nell'età moderna»
note: Downloaded in full (53 volumes, about 75 MB of text) and searched in September 2026. The bulk of «De Franceschi» hits are citations of Carlo and of his son Camillo as authorities; the scan reported here filtered those out and looked only for the surname standing near this family's places.

title: Dorotea Brhan, «Emigrazione dalla Carnia verso l'Istria (XVI–XIX sec.)»
where: Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, vol. XXXIV (2004), pp. 473–494
what: Twenty-two pages on the exact migration this family made, built from the parish and notarial books in the state archive at Pazin. It names the Cargnelli, distinguishes the pedlars from the home weavers, shows them buying vineyards in the eighteenth century and being written down as «D.no» for the first time — and lists a Dominus Vittorio De Franceschi among the Carnian landowners of Sanvincenti.

title: Egidio Ivetic, «La popolazione dell'Istria nell'età moderna. Lineamenti evolutivi»
where: Collana degli Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, n. 15 (1997), 450 pp.
what: The standard demographic history of early-modern Istria, counting hearths province by province from 1508. It gives Gallignana at a hundred and fifty hearths in 1508 — equal largest in the Habsburg county with Pisino — the collapse of the 1520s, and the trebling by the urbarium of 1571 that is the shape of the repopulation.

title: «Il Piccolo» di Trieste — the digitised run
what: The Trieste daily from 1881, issue by issue, with the full text indexed. title: Daniela Simon, «Die bedrohte Ordnung der Vielfalt. Kulturelle Hybridität in Istrien, 1870–1914»

title: Francesco Cavalli, «Della regione litorale Austro-Illirica»

title: Carlo De Franceschi, «Memorie autobiografiche», ed. Camillo De Franceschi

what: Carlo's autobiography, dictated as letters between April and December 1883 at the insistent asking of his son Gian Pietro, assistant judge at Pola, who died at thirty in 1884 and left the manuscript to his two brothers. Unpublishable under Austria; brought out by his son Camillo in 1926 with a preface, notes and appendices. Found and downloaded 7 September 2026 after this site had published that it did not hold it.

«Con tutti i suoi talenti ed i suoi meriti, condusse una vita stentata e morì povero»

what: A Venezuelan historian's history of the Corsican Franceschi of Ersa in Cap Corse, from Pietro Franceschi (1694–1771) to the emigration to Venezuela by way of the French Caribbean. title: «Atti» del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, vol. 39
what: Cites Camillo De Franceschi throughout as the authority on Pula, and yields his Pula bibliography — including «Testamenti polesani del secolo XV con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola», sixteen fifteenth-century wills he transcribed.

title: «Istra iz pera Nobilea» — Pietro Nobile's Istrian drawings

where: statueofliberty.org · free, no account, no paywall
what:

It aggregates seven American arrival collections — including **New York, Passenger Lists 1820–1920**, which covers the Castle Garden decades before Ellis Island opened, and the Vermont and Philadelphia border and port lists. Its records carry a **Last Residence** field, which is the field this archive most needs and which a name index alone never gives.

Two working notes for whoever comes after. **Use the exact-surname option**: the default is fuzzy and returns nine thousand rows of every spelling of Franceschi, while exact returns 204 and they are the right 204. And **the arrival-year filter does not work** — it changes the result count but not the rows returned, so a year-sliced harvest silently returns the same first page each time. Partition by name, not by year.

title: Milko Kos, «Doneski k zgodovini Istre v srednjem veku»
where: Vjesnik kr. hrvatsko-slavonsko-dalmatinskog zemaljskog arkiva 18, Zagreb 1916, p. 1 — free on Hungaricana
what:
**A correction to a source this archive leans on.** Kos publishes **twenty original parchment charters from the State Archive in Vienna (repertory 3)**, previously unpublished and unused, on the ministerial family styling itself *«de Pisino»* — and says plainly that his purpose is *«izpolniti in marsikje popraviti Franceschijeva izvajanja o genealogiji pazinskih gospodov»*: to fill out, and in many places correct, **Camillo De Franceschi's conclusions on the genealogy of the lords of Pazin**.

Camillo's *Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino* is on this archive's shelf and is cited across the site. So on 14 September 2026 **every statement on this site touching the medieval lords of Pazin was checked against it.** Nothing this archive claims depends on the part Kos corrects: the *«de Pisino»* were the ministeriales of the counts of Gorizia, **a different family entirely**, and what this site takes from Camillo is his work on the De Franceschi themselves and on the county's later history. The warning stands for the future rather than the past.

**And Camillo had said so himself.** Kos quotes him: *«con la scarsa messe di notizie che ci fu dato raccogliere intorno alla famiglia in discorso, non siamo purtroppo in grado di stabilirne la compléta e sicura genealogia»* — with the scanty harvest of information we were able to gather about the family in question, we are unfortunately not in a position to establish its complete and certain genealogy. **The family's own historian, declining to close a genealogy he could not prove.** This archive has no better sentence for what it is trying to do.
cites: Vjesnik 18 (Zagreb 1916), Sveska 1, p. 1 — Dr Milko Kos
Twenty unpublished parchments, Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv Vienna, repertory 3
Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino» — corrected in part

title: The National Archives, Kew — Discovery
where: Bessborough Road, Kew, Richmond TW9 4DU, United Kingdom
what:
The catalogue of the British national archive, and of some 2,500 other British archives besides. **It answers JSON to anybody, with no key and no account**: `discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/API/search/records?sps.searchQuery=<term>&sps.resultsPageSize=<n>`, returning `count` and a `records` list carrying `reference`, `title`, `coveringDates`, `heldBy` and a description. It throttles: sustained querying starts answering **HTTP 202 with an empty body**, and the polite response is to back off, which this archive did.

**Searched for the first time on 17 September 2026** and it holds nothing of this family — [the sweep and what it means](/research-log/). Its limit matters as much as its reach: Discovery indexes what has been catalogued down to the item, and for merchant shipping that is largely the ship and the year, so a master's name is not findable there even when his certificate is at Kew.

title: Österreichisches Staatsarchiv — Archivinformationssystem
what: The catalogue of the whole Austrian State Archives — Kriegsarchiv, Marine, Adelsarchiv, Hofkammer, Justiz — searchable by a free field search across every department, with no account. The last two are empty. **Catalogue only — no file has been ordered, and the Kriegsarchiv's EUR 45 search fee buys what this catalogue already names to the item.**

title: Findmypast
what: A paid British index, and after the Austrian catalogue the most productive single source this archive has used. It holds the American half of the family in documents — **the 1930 census with three of the Eleven in one Brooklyn flat**, Joseph's certificate of arrival (*Martha Washington*, out of Trieste, 11 October 1910, aged eighteen), Albina's 1928 petition in her own words (*«I emigrated from Genoa … on the vessel Conte Rosso»*), and Frank Schinkopan's 1920 declaration giving his birth at Pisino. Its British newspapers hold a whole chapter nobody knew was there: **between 1865 and 1878 a master of this name commands Austrian ships** in the Black Sea grain and Bristol Channel coal trades — the *Natalia*, the *Rachel*, the *Peppina Luigia*, the *Aquilone*.
note: **Paid. David took a one-month full subscription on 16 September 2026, and it ends.** *Transcripts and images are behind it; nothing is bought record by record.* **Its negatives are as useful as its hits:** *«Gallignana» returns ten records in the whole database and three are this family's; «Gallignana» in the British newspapers returns **zero**; the deaths of Bruno and Gerda are not in it, so their dates stay on the gravestone and the naturalisation papers.* **«Pisino» returns 915 articles and every one is OCR noise** — «early rising» mis-set, and a brand of stove polish.
cites: Findmypast — Travel & Migration, surname «defranceschi»

title: Google My Maps — David's own maps
what: Two maps David built himself over years, and a primary source in their own right rather than a reference work. Imported whole from the KML: **10 layers, 1,289 pins, 56 lines, 10 polygons, 111 notes and 188 links.** The 56 lines are **named movements drawn by hand** — *«Ivan moves to Senj»* and the like — which exist nowhere else. The emigration layers gave a departure region for the Brazilian cluster this archive had never had: **Scorzè, Moniego (Noale), Cornedo Vicentino, Castelgomberto and Pederobba** in the Veneto.
note: **A My Map dies with the account and no crawler saves one.** *An earlier JSON export kept the pins; only the KML kept the lines, polygons and notes.* **Both are now held here, which is the point of having taken them.**
cites: David's Google MyMaps — the emigration layers
David's Google My Map — imported whole from the KML

title: Gradska groblja Zagreb — the city burial register
what: Zagreb's municipal cemetery register, free and searchable, and unusually informative: **thirteen burials of the name, some carrying the parents' names.** *Milan Defrančeski (d. 2001, aged 78) and Dragutin (d. 2004, aged 79) are entered as children of «GRGO I MARIJA» and «MARIJA I GRGA»* — **two brothers naming the same father**, and that father is the Grga of David's old notes.
note: Free and open. *A burial register that names parents does work a death index cannot, and this one closed a relationship rather than merely recording a death.*
cites: Gradska groblja Zagreb — the city burial register

title: Hrvatski biografski leksikon
what: The Croatian biographical lexicon, which carries a full life of **«Defrančeski, Ante»** — born Ližnjan near Pula 1 February 1894, died Skrad 27 September 1949; Kastav teachers' college 1912; a volunteer on the Salonika front; Kotoriba and Čakovec 1920–24; the Higher Pedagogical School at Zagreb 1928; professor at the Zagreb teachers' training school; the Ministry of Education at Belgrade 1932–33.
note: Free and authoritative. *The **č** spelling is the one that finds him, and it is the spelling most of this archive's indexes cannot reach.*
cites: Hrvatski biografski leksikon — «Defrančeski, Ante»

title: Isidore — French humanities and social science search
what: A French aggregator of humanities scholarship, searched across the «Res pro Deo» journal collection for the surname and for twenty place-names.
note: **Zero, and usefully so.** *Every «De Franceschi» in five gigabytes of theology is a French historian of Jansenism, a Sienese printer, or a Venetian chancery secretary* — **none of them this family.** A large, clean negative on the scholarly literature.
cites: isidore.co «Res pro Deo» journal collection

title: Istarska enciklopedija (Leksikografski zavod Miroslav Krleža)
what: Bertoša's entry **«De Franceschi»** in the Istrian encyclopedia, and one of the few secondary works that treats this family directly. It carries the Agrons castle, the investitures of **1467 and 1471**, the **1502 «gismanus de Carnia»**, the *de Franciscus* at Mione in the sixteenth century, the **1661 first mention as «mistro Zuanne»**, the **1686 death of the «vecchio stipite»**, and the 1712 imprisonment of the parish priest.
note: Free. *This is the encyclopedia version; the footnoted scholarly original is Bertoša's «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa» in «Etos i etnos zavičaja» (1985), which this archive has not obtained.*
cites: Istarska enciklopedija (Bertoša), «De Franceschi»

title: OpenEdition Journals
what: The French open-access journal platform, read here for Pomara, **«An Attempted Albanian Settlement in Istria (1610–1612)»**, *Diasporas* 43 (2025).
note: **No person of the name.** *Carlo De Franceschi is cited as an authority — on the depopulation of Istria, and on Poreč falling to some three hundred souls by 1601* — **which is one more instance of the historian still being quoted, this time in 2025.** Nothing for the family.
cites: Pomara, «An Attempted Albanian Settlement in Istria (1610–1612)», Diasporas 43 (2025)

title: JUSP Jasenovac — Poimenični popis žrtava
what: The Jasenovac Memorial Site's published list of named victims of the Jasenovac and Stara Gradiška camps, free and searchable by surname. Searched on the surname and on both of Anka's married names.
note: **Nobody of this name is in it, in any spelling, and Anka is not in it under either married name.** *Defranceschi 0, Defranceski 0.* **A negative that had to be established rather than assumed**, and one this archive would rather have stated than left hanging over a family that lost people in those years.
cites: JUSP Jasenovac — the named victims list, on the surname and on both married names

title: Mémoire des Hommes · Grand Mémorial · Base Léonore
what: The French defence ministry's military personnel and casualty databases, together with the Grand Mémorial and the Légion d'honneur files — the obvious route into the French-side Defrance and Franceschi-Delonne names.
note: **Not searched.** *JavaScript applications with no reachable interface from here.* **Listed so that the gap is visible rather than silent.**
cites: Mémoire des Hommes, Grand Mémorial, Base Léonore

title: Muzej hrvatskih arheoloških spomenika, Split
what: The Museum of Croatian Archaeological Monuments, cited here for the 2000 exhibition catalogue **«Hrvati i Karolinzi»**, read by OCR.
note: **No person of the name, and none expected — the catalogue is about the ninth century.** *The surname appears three times and every one is **Camillo De Franceschi in the bibliography**, cited for his 1932 and 1933 work on the early-medieval church sculpture of Pula and Sv. Ivan.* **Recorded because a hit count of three, unexamined, would have looked like a family finding.**
cites: «Hrvati i Karolinzi» — the 2000 exhibition catalogue, OCR'd

title: Project MUSE
what: The Johns Hopkins scholarly platform, read here for *Nova et Vetera* 21:2 (2023).
note: **One footnote, citing Sylvio Hermann De Franceschi, a living French historian. Nothing else.** *Kept so the search is not run a second time.*
cites: «Nova et Vetera» 21:2 (2023)

title: Museu da Imigração do Estado de São Paulo
what: The Hospedaria de Imigrantes enrolment registers at São Paulo — the arrival record for the Brazilian cluster, and the natural companion to the Veneto departure region the My Maps gave.
note: **It was broken, and on 27 September 2026 it answers.** *Every query returned HTTP 500 on 21 September; six days later the same form returns **184 records** for the surname stem.* **The rows are substantial**, not an index stub: *Nome, Sobrenome, Nacionalidade, Idade, **Chegada** (the arrival date), **Parentesco** (CHEFE for a household head, SOZINHA for a woman travelling alone), **Família** (a family number that groups a household across the register) and **Livro**.* **The family number is the valuable field** — it is what turns a list of arrivals into households. *Nothing has been harvested yet, and the 184 include Franceschini and other names the stem catches, which are a different surname and must be separated before anything is counted.*
cites: Museu da Imigração / Hospedaria de Imigrantes, São Paulo, 21 September 2026

title: Pomorski i povijesni muzej Hrvatskog primorja, Rijeka
what: The Maritime and History Museum of the Croatian Littoral at Rijeka — the obvious holder for anything on the Fiume shipmasters of this name.
note: **The public search returns nothing for any spelling, and this is not a negative worth trusting.** *The interface is script-driven rather than searchable from here, and the museum holds **75,000 objects in 48 collections** of which the digital fundus is a fraction.* **The museum should be written to.**
cites: Pomorski i povijesni muzej Hrvatskog primorja, Rijeka

title: National Archives of Australia — RecordSearch
what: The free Australian federal archives catalogue, and the source that closed the question David asked about the child on the *General M B Stewart*: he is **Anton Mario De Franceski, born 21 August 1944 at Reutlingen**, Zdravko and Ruža's only child. Eight items of the name are catalogued, among them **A11534, 58–60** (1948), the household file carrying all three dates of birth, and **B44, V1978/151 and V1978/152**, Zdravko and Ruža's naturalisations.
note: **Free to search, and none of the eight is digitised.** *All eight have to be ordered, and two are still marked «not yet examined», which means an access decision before a copy.* **Catalogue-level certainty, file-level nothing** — the distinction this archive keeps insisting on, in its clearest form.
cites: National Archives of Australia — RecordSearch, NameSearch
National Archives of Australia — are any of the eight items digitised?

title: Google Scholar
what: Used to run down two scholarly works whose titles looked as though they might touch this family.
note: **Both are different families, and that is why they are recorded.** *Benedetti, «From Venice to Cairo» (2022), concerns **Andrea de' Franceschi**, Venetian grand chancellor, of Cividale di Belluno; Bruni, «Peace at the Lily» (2018), concerns **Francesco De Franceschi**, a printer «born in Siena around 1530».* **Three unrelated houses carry this name in the scholarship alone, which is the standing caution of a one-name study.**
cites: Benedetti, «From Venice to Cairo» (2022)
Bruni, «Peace at the Lily» (2018)

title: Stadtarchiv Reutlingen — photograph database
what: Reutlingen's city archive and its photograph database, worked for the German years. It identified **Hermann Sauer** as a motor-vehicle firm at the Südbahnhof / Eninger Landstraße 79, holding the MAN agency and running a filling station in the Marktstraße, and photographed **the Sauer brothers' Autohaus in the Tübinger Straße in 1935**.
note: Free, and it answers about places and firms rather than people. *This is the kind of source that turns a line on a form — an employer, a street — into somewhere that can be seen.*
cites: Stadtarchiv Reutlingen — photograph database

title: Trove — National Library of Australia
what: The free Australian newspaper and gazette portal. It gave **the last sighting of Zdravko alive** — *Commonwealth of Australia Gazette*, Periodic, No. P2, **16 February 1979, page 66**, under VICTORIA: «Defranceski, Roza, 19 Anderson St, Horsham 3400» — and one story: *The Age*, Melbourne, **25 January 1954**, «Girl Saw Friend Drown», naming **Giordano Defranceschi, laborer**.
note:
**Free, and it must be worked by spelling and by zone.** *The first pass ran newspapers only and only the fused spellings, reporting «Defranceski» 2 and «Defranceschi» 13; this archive's own rule — that each spelling returns a different, non-overlapping set — had not been applied to it.* **A Trove nil is usually weak:** *newspaper digitisation mostly stops in 1954, and whether the «Wimmera Mail-Times» is digitised for 1949–54 has never been established* — so the Horsham silence of the 1940s and 1950s proves much less than it appears to.

**An API key was issued to David on 27 September 2026, valid to December 2026, and it changes what this source is.** *The key is held at `private/trove.env`, which is gitignored — this repository is published, so a key committed here is a key published.*

**⚠ The finding that matters more than the key: Trove does NOT fold the space.** *FamilySearch returns the same 8,235 records for «Defranceschi» and «De Franceschi»; Findmypast folds it too. **Trove does not.** A quoted search for «Defranceschi» returns **13** newspaper articles and «De Franceschi» returns **128**, and **they overlap by three**.* **This archive's earlier Trove passes ran the fused spellings and reported 13, and were treating the source as swept.**

*Counted by the API across nine categories: **Defranceschi 73 · De Franceschi 393 · Defranceski 3 · De Franceski 6 · Franceski 34** — and the non-newspaper categories had never been searched at all: 176 books and 26 music entries sit under «De Franceschi» alone.* **All 170 distinct newspaper and gazette articles are now harvested to `data/harvest/trove-newspapers.json`.**

**One limit, stated so it is not rediscovered:** *the API returns metadata but **no OCR text** for gazettes — `wordCount` is given and `articleText` comes back empty at every `reclevel`. The text is on the public article page at `https://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article<id>`, which answers a plain request and is where the naturalisation names were read.*
cites: Trove — Australian newspapers, 1940–1959

title: The Internet Archive — Wayback Machine
what: Used for one job: to save the family's own Google Site at **defranceski.com** before it is switched off. A CDX query for every URL under that host returned **two successful captures** — the site root of 1 January 2022 and the home page of 11 July 2025.
note: **Nearly empty, and now filled.** *Family Trees, The People, The Places, The Map and The Name were never captured by any crawler.* **The lesson generalises: a site nobody links to is a site the Wayback Machine has not got**, and waiting for it to have done the job is not a preservation plan.
cites: The Wayback Machine — everything under sites.google.com/defranceski.com

title: Wikipedia
what: Cited in three languages, and in every case for a public figure rather than for this family's own people: **Carlo De Franceschi** on the Croatian and Czech Wikipedias, and **Piero della Francesca** at Sansepolcro and Monterchi on the English.
note: **Used as a pointer, never as evidence.** *Where a Wikipedia article states something this archive relies on, the article's own source is chased and cited instead.* The Carlo articles agree that he was born in 1809 at Moncalvo di Pisino, now Gologorica, into a family of small landowners — which the registers and the Istrian encyclopedia independently support.

note: **Recorded because the old site used them; this archive does not.** *They sell a crest to anyone who shares a surname, which is the opposite of what an arms attribution is.* **The arms page here rests on a lintel and a stone**, and the paper that would settle it is in the Adelsarchiv at Vienna, not on a shop.

note: **Linked without a comment on the old site.** *Secondary and unfootnoted; useful for names to chase, not for statements to cite.*

what: A long-running gateway of East European genealogical resources, linked for its Croatia page.
note: **Linked without a comment on the old site.** *A directory rather than a source; nothing here rests on it.*
cites: FEEFHS — Croatia (old site link list)

title: DVHH — Danube Swabian Heritage
what: The Danube Swabian heritage portal, linked from the old site.
note: **Linked without a comment, and off this family's ground** — *the Danube Swabian settlements are not where any line here runs.* Kept for completeness of the old site's record.
cites: DVHH — Danube Swabian Heritage (old site link list)

title: Smrikve — the Istrian local-history library
what: A large privately built library of west-Istrian local history. Linked here **on the other family's house at Seget** — the Rome-and-Candia line that left Crete when the Turks took it in 1669, and which is not this family.
note: **Substantial and useful, and about a different house.** *Recorded partly to keep that distinction visible: a Seget De Franceschi is not a Gračišće one.*
cites: Smrikve — Seget

title: Ministarstvo kulture i medija — Mala biblioteka Godišnjaka zaštite spomenika kulture
what: The Croatian culture ministry's publication series on monument protection; volume 20 (2019) is cited alongside Smrikve for the west-Istrian house at Seget.
note: **Free PDF, and about buildings rather than people.** *Cited for the fabric of a house, not for a family.*
cites: Mala biblioteka Godišnjaka zaštite spomenika kulture, sv. 20 (2019)

title: Istrapedia
what: The Istrian online encyclopedia, carrying a **«de Franceschi»** entry, cited here for Pićan — the Pedena where Antonio lived.
note: Free. *An encyclopedia entry is a pointer to the scholarship behind it, and this archive prefers Bertoša's Istarska enciklopedija article where the two overlap.*
cites: Istrapedia — «de Franceschi» (natuknica 628)

title: Istarsko povijesno društvo — članak br. 34
what: The Istrian Historical Society's PDF of article no. 34, linked from David's map against **Ližnjan**.
note: **Free PDF, carried over from the map and not yet read against this archive's Ližnjan people.** *Listed so that the reading is owed rather than forgotten.*
cites: Istarsko povijesno društvo, članak br. 34

title: Italian Parish Records
what: A guide to what Italian parish registers exist and where, linked from the map beside Antenati as the second door into Italy.
note: **A finding aid, not a record set.** *Free, and worth keeping for the Carnic parish question, where the Napoleonic civil registers stop in 1815 and the parish books are the only thing that reaches 1742.*

title: Università di Bologna — staff pages
what: Read in full for **Zelda Alice Franceschi**, a Bologna anthropologist of the Argentine Gran Chaco, because the surname and the Argentine subject together looked like a lead.
note: **No connection to this family.** *The surname is the author's own.* Recorded so the same coincidence is not chased twice.

what: A collaborative single-tree site, approached for profiles under this surname.
note: **Blocked by a bot check, not circumvented.**
cites: WikiTree — profile search

what: Used to locate two books this archive needs and does not have: **Vergé-Franceschi, «Le cap Corse: généalogies et destins» (2006)**, the reference work for Cap Corse families, which would settle whether the Tomino Defranceschi are in it; and **Bertoša, «Etos i etnos zavičaja» (Pula–Rijeka 1985)**, which contains «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa», the footnoted original behind the encyclopedia entry.

title: Patrimonio culturale — Regione Friuli Venezia Giulia
what: The regional cultural-heritage catalogue for Friuli Venezia Giulia. It holds drawings connected to this family's historians — illustrations for **«L'Istria nobilissima»**, material around Caprin's «Il Trecento a Trieste» (1897), and **a headpiece drawn for Camillo's Arcadia essay of 1929–30**.
note: **Free, and only half read.** *The individual sheet records remain unread.*
cites: Patrimonio culturale FVG — the drawings

title: Općina Žminj
what: The municipality of Žminj, whose local history carries the **«Carnielli» of Istria** — men described as *«...ra u Karniji»*, many still spending part of each year back at **Agrons near Ovaro**, and marrying only girls from there, who stayed in Carnia while the men wintered in Istria.
note: **This is the clearest local statement of the pattern this whole archive is trying to document** — *a seasonal Carnic presence in Istria that becomes a settled one.* Secondary, and it points straight at Ovaro, which the Antenati survey independently reached.
cites: Općina Žminj — the Carnielli of Istria

title: Nati in Trentino
what: The Trentino provincial index of parish baptisms, which would cover the Trentino spellings of the name.
note: **Behind an operator login — «accesso dell'operatore» — and the public site search returns «Nessun risultato».** *Not circumvented.* **A written request to the Servizio coesione territoriale at Trento is the route.**
cites: Nati in Trentino

title: NSW State Archives — passenger lists
what: The New South Wales passenger indexes, free to search. They gave the earliest Australian appearance of the name: an arrival on **6 January 1893** — **a sailor passing through, not an emigrant**.
note: **Free, and it fixes a date this archive had wrong by two generations.** *The surname reaches Australia in 1893 at sea, and does not settle there for another fifty-seven years.*
cites: NSW State Archives — passenger lists

title: Villa Ružić, Rijeka — the de Canziani Jakšić collection
what: A private Rijeka archive and house museum, approached over the Hotel Therapia at Crikvenica — where Hedviga Blažević is said to have sung, and to have met Ivan Defranceski.
note: **A full and generous answer, and the answer is that the paper is gone.** *Martina Riedl of the Kvarner Palace — the former Therapia, Austrian-owned since 2004 — replies that almost nothing survives from the period asked about.* **The story stands where it stood: as testimony, uncorroborated, and now with the hotel's own archive formally eliminated as a route to it.**
cites: Hotel Kvarner Palace, Crikvenica — the former Hotel Therapia

title: Istria Outside My Window
what: Isabel Putinja's Istrian blog, carrying **«A peek inside Gračišće's Salamon Palace» (2018)** — photographs of the interior, and **the only published look inside that this archive knows of**.
note: *Photographs, credited to their author and not reproduced here.* **The house on Gračišće's square is the one drawn on the direct line, which makes this the nearest thing to a view of it.**
cites: Istria Outside My Window — «A peek inside Gračišće's Salamon Palace» (2018)

title: Istra.hr — the Istrian tourist board
what: Cited for **«Istrian building heritage of the Venetian era»**, which supplies the architectural description quoted on the direct line — **and the point that Gračišće was never Venetian**.
note: *A tourist-board page used for one architectural statement, which is checked against Huić's «Urbanistički razvoj Gračišća u Istri», Prostor 23 (2015) 2.*
cites: Istra.hr — «Istrian building heritage of the Venetian era»
